draft.title: How flows of water connect places
card: Rivers and groundwater carry water from one place to another. Rivers flow downhill from upstream to downstream, and groundwater moves slowly through soil and rock.
Moving water also carries other things: sediment (soil and sand), nutrients and pollution. These can travel a long way from where they started.
So what happens upstream can change places downstream. Taking water, clearing land or adding pollution upstream can change the amount and quality of water further down.
The Murray-Darling Basin is an example. Its rivers join many towns, farms and wetlands across several states, so the use of water in one part can affect people and ecosystems in another.
draft.remember: Water flows carry more than water, so upstream actions can affect downstream places.

a.q: Why can a farm upstream affect a town downstream on the same river?
opts: The river carries water and anything in it downstream
The river carries only water, so the farm has no effect
Groundwater always moves upstream from the town
Rivers stop flowing once they pass a farm
a.why: A river moves water and also sediment, nutrients and pollution from upstream to downstream. The town can therefore be affected by what the farm takes or adds. A river carrying only water would not link the places in this way.
a.clue: Think about what a river carries besides water.

b.q: Heavy soil erosion upstream sends a lot of sediment into a river. Which change is most likely in a wetland downstream?
opts: The water becomes muddier as sediment arrives
The water becomes clearer as sediment stays upstream
The wetland is unaffected, as sediment cannot travel
The wetland dries up because sediment adds water
b.why: Moving water carries sediment downstream, so the wetland receives muddier water. The idea that the wetland is unaffected is wrong because flows connect places. Sediment does not add water.
b.clue: Where does sediment go once the river picks it up?

wants.why: A map shows how one river system links many places across several states.
